parameters.query:
SELECT s.token, u.id AS user_id, u.name, u.email, u.role, u.active,
  u.theme_header_color, u.theme_main_color, u.theme_accent_color
FROM sessions s
JOIN users u ON u.id = s.user_id
WHERE s.token = $1 AND s.expires_at > now()
LIMIT 1;

nodes.name: Build Verdict
nodes.notes: Single source of truth every caller reads via $('Verify Session').item.json.{valid, userId, role}. A row only exists here if the token was actually issued at login and hasn't expired — unlike the old token_<id>_<timestamp> format, this can't be forged.
